Figure 1:High-fidelity mesh reconstruction without per-scene optimization.Our method takes multi-view images as input and directly outputs a high-resolution mesh
with mesh flow models. We adopt a coarse-to-fine cascade: the entire scene is generated
at a coarse resolution first, and regions of interest are then upscaled. The cascade
layout and the mesh resolution are chosen at inference time. Colors mark the cascade
level each surface was generated at.

Figure 2:Method overview.Lnndenotes levelnn.(a)DA3 points place the L0
cells and select their views. Each finer level halves the cell size and refines the mesh of the
level above.(b)Each image is encoded once as a tile pyramid, and from each view a cell
takes the tiles at the pyramid level that matches its voxel spacing.(c)All cells at all
levels share the SS and mesh generators, which attend to these tiles. At finer levels, the SS
stage starts from the noised parent (SDEdit).

Figure 6:Effect of image conditioning.The baseline uses the GenRecon-style conditioner, our voxel-queried attention replaces it, and the ConvNeXt branch is then added, all at the finest cascade level. show a synthetic multi-room house, and the last two show procedural grass
scenes.

Figure 21:Effect of image conditioning on Tanks and Temples.Meshes at the finest cascade level from the 4K images, all rendered from the same viewpoint per scene. The baseline uses the GenRecon-style conditioner, our voxel-queried attention replaces it, and the ConvNeXt branch is then added.

Figure 22:Effect of the synthetic training data.Meshes at the finest cascade level with 32 input views, from the model trained with our synthetic multi-room houses and grass scenes (Full) and from one trained on SAGE-10K and 3D-FRONT alone (w/o house & grass). Without the synthetic data, walls of the multi-room ScanNet++ scene disappear, and the grass around the loader becomes a flat surface.
